keyed lookup of an absent or null key is null; a `-key` sorted/index iterates descending (rev ascending); inserting an existing key replaces it; `#remove` and `c[key] = null` remove by key leaving the rest
a text returned from an element, a nested-slice element or a closure-mutated captured parameter is delivered before the callee's stores go (values here; tests/returned_text_lifetime.rs arms poison)
12000 single appends keep every element and leave the store a handful of free blocks (growth by doubling, not per append)
native-compile regression: a `#rust` native's text result passed straight on as a text argument; assertions pin only a non-empty report and its prefix
`c[key] = v` inserts or replaces on hash/sorted/index (also through a `&` param and a field); `+= [rec]` with a present key replaces, latest wins, order kept
`#remove` inside a bounded, open, reversed or descending keyed range removes exactly the chosen records and the walk visits exactly the range
bounded generics (Numeric, Addable, Equatable, Ordered, Printable) compute with the operators and methods their bounds supply, unary and binary, derived comparisons included
a mutation through a captured heap parameter reaches the caller; a captured scalar parameter's rebind reaches the enclosing slot; a captured `&` parameter writes back
records fetched lazily from a store image carry the written values; the resident counts (fetch on miss only), one record per key, absent-vs-unreachable and sticky faults have no formal rule yet
a lazily traversed person->company graph over two store images reads the written values; the identity and fetch-count properties have no formal rule yet

a keyed collection bound to a lazy source fetches a record only on a MISS, holds one record per key (a later hit or query reaches the same record), and tells an absent key (no error) from an unreachable source (a sticky error until cleared); collections.md
a lazy binding is per collection (two struct fields on one table are two bindings) and an explicit query fills the bound collection; same proposed rule as 129-lazy-sql-graph; collections.md
an explicit lazy query and a keyed lookup reach the SAME record (identity), a predicate matching nothing is not an error, one that cannot run is; same proposed rule; collections.md
a lazy key range on an ordered kind is one query that places records by key and adds only what is new; a hash refuses a range; same proposed rule; collections.md
one lazy lookup against a database reports the value or the refusal reason; same proposed rule; collections.md
map/filter/reduce answer their comprehension's values (empty in, empty out; init respected); a struct callback parameter edits the caller's record while the results are fresh records
two headers spelling `T` with different bounds are two variables, each satisfied by its own signature (arity, parameter type, return type, operator arity), while identical bounds still share

`xs[i] = Cont { m: cm }` and `xs[i] = mkc(7)` hand each element its own nested vector (every element keeps its values)

a paged prefix query against one trie image loads records for each prefix (the driver reads the fetch counts)
the layout pass renumbers trie nodes and no answer moves: key order, exact lookup, an absent key and the prefix walk agree fresh and reloaded

the program's entry is the ENTRY file's `main`; a `main` declared in a used module is an ordinary function of that module and never displaces it; calls.md

a view dead before a removal keeps its alias and writes through; one live across a removal (if, loop, read-after) is copied and its write stays in the copy
projecting a record-returning call's field (chained, depth three, two temps, in a loop, as an argument) runs each OpDrop hook exactly once, ids traced

an inline construction in a tuple member runs its hook once through the element free (values under poison: tests/store_lifetime_1512_1513.rs)
a record bound from a call that borrows a const argument answers the same whether viewed or copied; a written, escaping, captured, returned or rebound-base local is a copy and the source stays intact

a struct-literal tail built into the caller's buffer still answers a fresh value per call (escaping into a vector/field, surviving a later call, reassigned); `u = a` copies; omitted fields take their default every call

a vector slice is a fresh vector in every value position — a const or by-value argument, a return, an if arm, a field value, a literal element, a nested call, a generic instance; clamped and empty slices too
a mapped file presents as an ordinary `vector<u8>` that answers every read (len, index, iteration, slice, text_from_bytes) exactly as the copying read does; a bind of it copies
a slice of a mapped file is a view answering what the copy answers, through nested views, after the handle is rebound or gone, under par; a field stores a copy; a bind copies
an early return above several body-scoped vector locals answers its value and the other path reads all three vectors intact (leak gate: nothing leaked)

a file operation that cannot complete (missing or unopenable file, unwritable target) answers its own failure value - a read null, a write a FileResult other than Ok, exists false - and continues, never a runtime error; paths.md (Path-Refuse states this only for refused paths)
text + character joins; mutually recursive calls each get their own frame (first/second -> 12); the labelled-loop half (i#break, i#continue) has no formal rule
a slice match over a coroutine subject: a scalar repetition is the typed rest, a variant repetition collects, ..rest takes what is left
